title: Back-and-forth: partial isomorphisms and countable structures

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory

summary: Build isomorphisms by extending finite matches in both directions, and use countable categoricity to prove completeness.
abstract: Any two nonempty countable dense linear orders without endpoints can be matched one element at a time. Each finite match preserves the order, and alternating between the two sets eventually reaches every element on both sides. The same construction works for nonempty countable first-order structures when a finite match exists and the allowed matches can always be extended in both directions. To connect uniqueness of models with logical truth, we use downward Löwenheim–Skolem: for a satisfiable theory in a countable language with no finite models, if all countably infinite models are isomorphic, then every model gives the same answers to first-order sentences.
